best_for: Makers, engineers and students who need parametric 3D CAD for parts and assemblies and cannot or will not pay for a commercial license.
description:
FreeCAD is a 3D design program for objects that will be built in the real world, made by the FreeCAD Team and backed by the FreeCAD project association in Belgium, which collects donations and sponsorships. Its geometry engine is Open CASCADE Technology.

You can work in microns, inches, feet or a mix, and the units stay exact. Round edges with fillets, combine or cut solids, then turn your model into 2D drawings with views for the workshop. When the design is done, export it for a 3D printer or a CNC machine, or pull out a bill of materials and part quantities. Add-on workbenches from the community extend it, for example with other ways to assemble parts.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: FreeCAD is LGPL software built by a community with no commercial aim. The files you make are yours, and there is no account or subscription.

points.title: Change a number, the model follows
points.text: Shapes are driven by properties and constraints. Edit a dimension and the model recalculates, while undo and redo keep your history.

points.title: Workbenches for each job
points.text: Sketcher feeds Part Design, and there are workbenches for 2D drafting, surfaces, BIM, CAM toolpaths, finite element analysis and, since 1.0, assemblies with 3D constraints.

points.title: Talks to other CAD tools
points.text: It imports and exports STEP, IGES, STL, OBJ, DXF, DWG, SVG and IFC, so you can trade files with shops and other programs. Python scripting and macros let you automate the dull steps.

points.title: Needs a 64-bit, current system
points.text: Builds are 64-bit only. Windows needs 10 or later and macOS needs 12 Monterey or later, with separate Intel and Apple silicon images. Linux gets an AppImage or the Flatpak.

points.title: Weekly builds are for testing
points.text: The community publishes weekly development builds. The project warns they are less stable and use more memory, so keep backups if you try one.

points.title: Plan for the disk space
points.text: The Flatpak is verified on Flathub, for x64 and Arm64, and takes about 1.3 GB once installed. The Windows listing keeps 18 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
